title: A comeback at the counter
purpose: What an advisor does and says when a customer returns with the same problem.
facts: Six counter steps; the new order is of type warranty tied to the original (design 2.3).

Outcome table: our fault inside warranty = free; outside warranty = goodwill decided by slot 4 or 22; a different fault = estimate, no charge for the look; customer's part = labour charged again; unsure = slot 4 the same day.
A comeback inspection is never charged.
A second comeback on the same repair goes to slot 4 or slot 22 with both orders (A5's two vans came back at west: S1, S6).

rows.What he found: Our work or our part, inside the warranty
rows.What happens: Fixed at no charge. Say so before they ask. Offer the shuttle
Greg or Dale decides. Usually we fix it: goodwill order

rows.What he found: A different fault with the same symptom
rows.What happens: Explain with the old part or a photo. Estimate like any job. No charge for the look
Labour is charged again. This was said at the start; say it kindly
It is Greg's call, not yours. The same day

list_items.item: "Thank you for bringing it straight back." Mean it. The ones who do not come back are the ones we lose.
Find the first order. Read what was done and who did it before you say anything about the cause.
Open a new order, type warranty, tied to the first one. Do not reopen the old order and do not write it up as a new customer-pay job "until we know".
It goes to the front of the line. The foreman looks first: When a car comes back.
Tell the customer when they will hear: today, with a time.
Do not guess the cause at the counter and do not blame the part, the technician or the customer. "We will find out and I will call you by two."

new_facts: The look at a comeback is free; second comebacks escalate.
